## Call to impeach Judge Boasberg (March 2025)

In March 2025, Musk said it was "necessary" to file impeachment articles against U.S. District Judge [[james-boasberg|James E. Boasberg]], who had halted deportations of alleged [[tren-de-aragua|Tren de Aragua]] members ordered by President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] under the [[alien-enemies-act|Alien Enemies Act]].[n] The endorsement took the form of a one-word quote-tweet — "necessary" — posted in response to a legislator discussing proposed impeachment legislation, after Boasberg ruled on Saturday, March 15 that immediate action was needed because the government had already begun removing individuals under Trump's executive proclamation.[n] Badlands commentator [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] noted that the single-word post spawned a full news article giving a play-by-play of the exchange, remarking that "every Elon tweet cannot be a 500-word news article" and that legacy outlets reduced to diagramming tweets were broken.[n]

## Move to dismiss Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar (March 2025)

On Sunday, March 16, 2025, Netanyahu announced his intention to dismiss [[shin-bet|Shin Bet]] chief [[ronen-bar|Ronen Bar]], summoning him to an urgent evening meeting and informing him that the cabinet would vote on his removal later that week; the attorney general responded that no dismissal could proceed before a legal review.[n] Netanyahu said in a video statement that "at all times, but especially during an existential war such as the one we face, there must be full trust between the prime minister and the head of the Shin Bet," declaring an "ongoing distrust" that had grown over time while professing appreciation for the service's personnel.[n]

The move followed Netanyahu's police report the previous week alleging that former Shin Bet director [[nadav-argaman|Nadav Argaman]] was blackmailing him after Argaman cryptically threatened in an interview to expose truths about Netanyahu and the October 7 attack.[n] Badlands commentator [[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] wrote that Argaman had cited Netanyahu's exposed funding of [[hamas|Hamas]] in 2018–19 after the group lost Palestinian Authority backing, a factor said to have cost Netanyahu moderate Zionist support and pushed him toward Kahanist coalition partners, and that Bar had signaled willingness to further expose those ties through a report showing the money originated in [[qatar|Qatar]].[n] The same commentary raised the question of whether Netanyahu had been involved in planning the October 7 attack, noting its convenient timing as he faced pressure to normalize relations with Palestine and accept a two-state solution he had long opposed, and reported that he was attempting to sabotage [[adam-boehler|Adam Boehler]]'s effort to free American hostages.[n]

## March 2025: Yemen strikes, deportations, and Canada pressure

On March 15–16, 2025, Trump launched large-scale military strikes against Yemen's Iran-aligned [[houthis|Houthis]] over their attacks on Red Sea shipping, killing at least 31 people at the start of a campaign expected to last many days, and warned [[iran|Iran]] that it must immediately halt support for the group, saying "America will hold you fully accountable and, we won't be nice about it!"[n] Over the same weekend his administration invoked the [[alien-enemies-act|Alien Enemies Act]] to deport hundreds of alleged [[tren-de-aragua|Tren de Aragua]] members, proceeding despite an order from Judge [[james-boasberg|James Boasberg]] blocking the law's use and directing planes in the air to return.[n] He was also expected to speak with [[vladimir-putin|Vladimir Putin]] that week about ending the war in Ukraine, following envoy [[steve-witkoff|Steve Witkoff]]'s "positive" Moscow meeting.[n]

Trump's pressure on [[canada|Canada]] dominated the first foreign trip of new prime minister [[mark-carney|Mark Carney]], who sought alliances in Paris and London while insisting Canada would "never, ever, in any way shape or form, be part of the United States"; Trump had posted in December that no one could explain why the United States subsidizes Canada "to the tune of over $100,000,000 a year" and suggested many Canadians would prefer statehood.[n] In a lighter incident at Joint Base Andrews, a wind-muffling "dead cat" microphone struck Trump in the lip and cheek as he leaned in to hear a question about freeing more hostages from Gaza; he glared briefly at the reporter before joking that "she just made television tonight," and the operator was heard apologizing.[n]
